## Individual summaries

_summarizeInds()_: This function will produce a summary of genotyping across individuals, including the number of loci genotyped for each, the number and percent of loci missing genotypes, and the percent of loci homozygous.
```{r}
ind.smry <- summarizeInds(msats.g)

head(ind.smry)

tail(ind.smry)
```

## Allelic diversity

There are several by-locus summary functions available for _gtypes_ objects. Given some sample microsatellite data:
```{r}
data(msats.g)
msats <- stratify(msats.g, "broad")
msats <- msats[, getLociNames(msats)[1:4], ]
```

One can compute the following summaries:

_numAlleles()_: The number of alleles at each locus with:
```{r}
numAlleles(msats)
```

_numMissing()_: The number of samples with missing data at each locus:
```{r}
numMissing(msats)
```
which can also be expressed as a proportion of samples with missing data:
```{r}
numMissing(msats, prop = TRUE)
```

_allelicRichness()_: The allelic richness, or the average number of alleles per sample:
```{r}
allelicRichness(msats)
```

_heterozygosity()_: Both observed and expected heterozygosity:
```{r}
# observed
heterozygosity(msats, type = "observed")

# expected
heterozygosity(msats, type = "expected")
```

_propUniqueAlleles()_: The proportion of alleles that are unique (present in only one sample):
```{r}
propUniqueAlleles(msats)
```

These measures are all calculated in the _summarizeLoci()_ function and returned as a matrix. This function also allows you to calculate the measures for each stratum separately, which returns a list for each stratum. Many of these functions have a _by.strata_ argument. See the help file of each for details.
```{r}
summarizeLoci(msats)
summarizeLoci(msats, by.strata = TRUE)
```

_thetaH_: The package also calculates theta~H~, the population scaled mutation rate based on heterozygosity using several models:
```{r}
thetaH(msats, model = 'IAM')

thetaH(msats, model = 'SMM')

thetaH(msats, model = 'ZourosSMM')
```

_alleleFreqs()_: One can also obtain the allelic frequencies for each locus overall and by-strata by:
```{r}
alleleFreqs(msats)

af <- alleleFreqs(msats, by.strata = TRUE)
str(af)
```

The _dupGenotypes()_ function identifies samples that have the same or nearly the same genotypes. The number (or percent) of loci that must be shared in order for it to be considered a duplicate can be set by the _num.shared_ argument. The return data.frame provides which loci the two samples show mismatches at so they can be reviewed.
```{r}
# Find samples that share alleles at 2/3rds of the loci
dupes <- dupGenotypes(msats, num.shared = 0.66)
head(dupes)
```
